notes: Subject insert. 'Scots is a West Germanic language' is a class assertion, with West Germanic under Germanic (definitional, firm). q1 ('a Celtic language?', no) needs Scots to be the word's only language, the closed-world step the record's chain states: a nominal, glendrink : word_of_language only {scots} (firm). q3 ('the same branch of the Germanic family') is a join through the branch individual (instance_of, branches as individuals beside the language classes); Scots and English are West Germanic (firm bridges). Both relabelled dl on 2026-10-31 (COVERAGE.md label corrections); the fol section keeps its Z3 encoding as a second check. 2026-10-31: the closed world for 'glendrink' (glendrink : word_of_language only {scots}) is part of the edit (the edit names one language), not a background belief: as a firm background item it answered the questions without the edit (justify.py no_edit).
